title: Hiding From The One Who Loves Us

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then the man and his wife heard the sound of the Lord God as he was walking in the garden in the cool of the day, and they hid from the Lord God among the trees of the garden. — Gen 3:8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
There is something deeply sad in this verse. The sound of God walking in the garden was once, surely, the sweetest sound Adam and Eve knew — the nearness of the God who made them and loved them. But now that same sound sends them scrambling to hide among the trees.

Sin does this. It doesn't only make us feel ashamed of ourselves; it changes how we see God. The One who came to walk with them now feels like Someone to run from. Yet notice — God had not changed at all. He still came, still walked, still sought them out in the cool of the day, just as before. The distance was entirely on their side.

Isn't this often true of us? When we have sinned, our instinct is to pull away from God — to skip prayer, to avoid His Word, to hide among the "trees" of busyness or distraction. We imagine God is now against us, when in truth He is still coming near, still seeking us.

Dear friend, the good news is that God does not wait for us to find our way back. He comes looking. That same seeking heart would one day walk this earth in Jesus, who came "to seek and to save the lost" (Lk 19:10). We hide, but He still comes. And He comes not to condemn, but to restore.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When you sin, is your instinct to run to God or to hide from Him?
2. What "trees" do you tend to hide behind when guilt weighs on you?
3. How does it change things to know that God comes seeking you rather than waiting for you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, forgive me for the times I have hidden from You instead of running to You. Thank You that in Jesus You came seeking the lost, and that You still draw near even when I want to pull away. Help me to come out of hiding and walk with You again. Amen.
